title: Platform Systems & Services — Team Wiki, How‑Tos, Dashboards & Runbooks (Q2 2026)
author: Riley Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: Single canonical team wiki page that consolidates the Platform Systems & Services inventory, common how-tos, recommended dashboards / alerting, runbooks for operational incidents, recent retrospectives, and the short-term roadmap. Audience: platform engineers, SREs, on-call, and platform product managers.

Scope
- Services covered: control-plane services, routing & inference gateways, caching/batcher, observability ingestion, and platform support tooling.
- Environments: staging, prod-us, prod-eu (private deployments may have additional entries in eng-private-deployments).

1) Systems & Services inventory (summary)
| Service | Owner | Primary SLO | Key alerts | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| platform-api | platform-api-team@redwood.com | Availability 99.95% / p99 latency < 200ms | high-error-rate, high-latency | REST/GraphQL public & internal admin APIs |
| model-router | serving-runtime-team@redwood.com | Availability 99.9% / tail latency < 250ms | router-drops, model-oom | Routes requests to dedicated pools and hosted nodes |
| inference-runtime | runtime-team@redwood.com | Availability 99.9% / token-tp > 20k tok/s per-GPU | gpu-oom, kvcache-miss-spike | Optimized kernels, quantization variants |
| kv-cache | infra-team@redwood.com | Hit-rate > 85% for prefix workloads | cache-evictions, redis-high-latency | Redis cluster + LRU sharding |
| batcher | infra-team@redwood.com | Throughput target: 95% requests batched within 30ms window | batching-latency, queue-growth | Controls dynamic batching config |
| obs-ingest | observability-team@redwood.com | Metrics/Tracing retention SLA (99.9% ingestion) | high-drop-rate, write-latency | Prometheus + Cortex + Tempo |

2) How‑tos (common procedures)
A. Deploy a new platform API version (canary rollout)
1. Create release branch and build container: `make build && docker build -t ghcr.io/redwood/platform-api:$REV`
2. Push image and create image-policy in ECR/GCR.
3. Update Canary k8s deployment (namespace: platform-canary):
   kubectl -n platform-canary set image deployment/platform-api platform-api=ghcr.io/redwood/platform-api:$REV
4. Verify health checks: `kubectl -n platform-canary get pods -l app=platform-api` and check /healthz and /metrics.
5. Run smoke tests: `./scripts/smoke_tests.sh --target canary` (must pass: auth, health, basic generation).
6. Monitor canary for 30 minutes; if signals (error-rate > 0.5% or p95 latency increase > 20%), rollback: `kubectl -n platform-canary rollout undo deployment/platform-api`
7. If stable, promote to prod using gradual rollout by patching deployment replicas and scaling up by 10% every 10 minutes until desired capacity.

B. Add a new Grafana dashboard for a service
- Template: use `platform-dashboard-template.json` in team repo.
- Steps: duplicate template, set datasource to Prometheus (prod-prom), update panel queries to service-specific metrics, add annotations for deploys. Commit to `infra/grafana/dashboards`. CI will validate and publish to Grafana.

C. Onboarding a new on-call engineer
- Checklist: read runbook, add to PagerDuty schedule, run through a game-day (see section 5), ensure 2FA + Okta access, verify Slack incident channel membership.

3) Dashboards & alerting (recommended metrics and concrete thresholds)
Core dashboards (all services should expose these panels):
- Availability & errors: 5m error rate, 1h error trend, error-by-endpoint.
- Latency distributions: p50/p95/p99, histogram for token latency.
- Capacity and resource utilization: GPU utilization, queue length, free GPU memory.
- Batching & cache: batch size distribution, batching latency, cache hit ratio.
- Infra health: pod restarts, OOM kills, node pressure (cpu/mem/iops).

Recommended alerts (Prometheus examples)
1) High error rate (page):
- Expr: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=~\"platform-api|model-router\",status!~\"2..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=~\"platform-api|model-router\"}[5m])) > 0.01`
- For: 5m
- Severity: page
- Runbook: run `platform-api diagnostics` (see Runbooks section), check recent deploys, check canary.

2) High tail latency (page for customer-impacting):
- Expr: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~\"platform-api|model-router\"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.25`
- For: 5m

3) GPU OOM / low GPU memory (page):
- Expr: `node_gpu_memory_free_bytes / node_gpu_memory_total_bytes < 0.12`
- For: 1m

4) Cache miss spike (page):
- Expr: `increase(kv_cache_misses_total[5m]) > 1000 and (increase(kv_cache_misses_total[5m]) / increase(kv_cache_requests_total[5m])) > 0.25`
- For: 5m

Alert labeling conventions
- Labels: severity=page|ticket, team=platform|serving-runtime|infra, service=<service-name>, runbook=<runbook-id>.
- PagerDuty routing: severity=page => primary on-call. severity=ticket => routed to team queue.

4) Runbooks (incident triage and resolution)
Generic incident triage (high-level)
1. Triage (first 5 min): confirm alert, determine blast radius (region(s), tenants affected), set incident channel on Slack `#inc-<service>-<YYYYMMDD>`, assign incident commander (IC).
2. Gather telemetry: check Grafana dashboards, query traces (Tempo), check recent deploys, check PagerDuty notes and rate of incoming alerts.
3. Mitigation: apply fast mitigations (scale up, fail-over to read-only, route to fallback model variant).
4. Root cause analysis: capture logs, core dumps, stack traces, correlate with infra events.
5. Recovery & postmortem: when service restored, run RCA and file postmortem in `oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems` within 72 hours.

Runbook: model-router high-drop-rate
- Symptoms: `router_request_dropped_total` increase, 5xx rate increase on platform-api, customers reporting truncated responses.
- Immediate steps:
  1. Verify backpressure metrics: `sum(rate(router_dropped_total[1m]))` and per-pool queue length.
  2. Check downstream capacity: `kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide` for inference-runtime pool health.
  3. If a particular model pool is overloaded, fallback: update routing override `kubectl -n serving apply -f routing-override.yaml` (example in repo).
  4. If OOMs present, evacuate nodes: `kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets` and request infra to reprovision.
  5. After stabilization, roll a hotfix to adjust batching/window parameters.

5) Recent retrospective (last 90 days) — summary & action items
Incident summary: 2026-01-18 model-router partial outage (3 hours) caused by a batching change that increased tail latency and induced cascading backpressure on platform-api.
Root cause: an untested batching policy was deployed to prod which increased the batching window from 30ms -> 200ms under low-QPS workloads.
Action items:
- (Done) Add pre-deploy synthetic tests for batching window changes (PR: infra/ci#237).
- (In progress) Enforce canary minimum traffic floor for batching-related changes. Owner: Noor Singh. ETA: 2026-03-15.
- (Planned) Dashboard: batching window vs p99 latency correlation panel. Owner: observability-team. ETA: 2026-03-10.

6) Roadmap (next 90 days)
Short-term (Q2 2026):
- Platform observability: rollout of traced request-id propagation and higher-fidelity sampling for model-router (owner: observability). Target: 2026-04-30.
- Runbooks: centralize runbooks into a searchable playbook index and enable the incident CLI to fetch runbooks by alert label (owner: eng-platform). Target: 2026-05-15.
- Autoscale improvements: integrate GPU bin-packing heuristics to reduce cold start latency (owner: infra). Target: 2026-06-01.
Medium-term:
- Standardize SLO configs in GitOps (one YAML per service) and validate them through CI.
- Expand canary orchestration to include synthetic load generators.

7) Team wiki & contribution process
- Single source of truth: this page is the entry point. Service-specific runbooks live in `confluence/eng-platform/<service>-runbook-YYYY.json` and source-of-truth configs live in `infra/` repos.
- Document template: use `platform-doc-template.md` (header includes Title, Owner, SLOs, Alerts, Runbook, How-to, Related pages).
- Change process: PRs to this wiki should be reviewed by at least one owner and one SRE. Major changes (SLO/alert threshold changes) require an advisory review from Observability and Product.
- Ownership: every service must have a declared owner in the metadata header (see inventory table).

8) Appendix — snippets and examples
A. Prometheus alert rule example (YAML)
```
groups:
- name: platform.rules
  rules:
  - alert: PlatformHighErrorRate
    expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=~"platform-api|model-router",status!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=~"platform-api|model-router"}[5m])) > 0.01
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: page
      team: platform
    annotations:
      summary: "High error rate on platform-api or model-router"
      runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/platform-runbook-high-error-rate-2026.json"
```

B. Grafana panel snippet (JSON skeleton)
```
{
  "title": "p99 latency (platform-api)",
  "targets": [{ "expr": "histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job='platform-api'}[5m])) by (le))" }]
}
```

C. CLI quick commands
- Check on-call: `pagerduty whoami`
- Query recent traces for request-id: `tempo query --id <request-id>`
- Evacuate node: `kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

Questions / edits
- If you find missing runbooks or an incorrect owner, file a PR or ping @platform-team on Slack.

References
- See `eng-platform/platform-systems-services-playbook-2026.json` for the canonical playbook.
- Oncall & incident process: `oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process`.
